# FDG4032

> DO implement `IEquatable<T>` on value types.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 4.7 Struct Design.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG4032
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Implement IEquatable<{0}> on the value type '{0}'

FDG4032 reports an externally visible struct, other than a ref struct, that does not implement IEquatable<T> of itself; record structs implement it already. Structs that are not externally visible are not checked. CA1815 is not mapped: it also asks for the equality operators, which this rule does not (section 8.6 covers equality). There is no code fix: Equals and GetHashCode need the type's own notion of equality.

## From the book

The `Object.Equals` method on value types causes boxing, and its default implementation is not very efficient, because it uses reflection. `IEquatable<T>.Equals` can have much better performance and can be implemented so that it will not cause boxing. See section 8.6 for guidelines on implementing `IEquatable<T>`.
